thread.title: World Bank urges agro-industrialization for sustainable economic growth in Uganda
thread.title_full: World Bank urges agro-industrialization for sustainable economic growth in Uganda

author: Globe Banner
title: World Bank urges agro-industrialization for sustainable economic growth in Uganda
text:
Uganda’s economy continued to grow in the fiscal year 2024/2025, with real GDP rising to 6.3% from 6.1% the previous year, according to a new World Bank report. The increase is attributed to a recovery in household consumption, higher government spending, and ongoing investment growth.
The latest Uganda Economic Update from the World Bank highlights that growth was broad-based across agriculture, industry, and services sectors. As a result, poverty levels are projected to have declined during this period. The report also notes that inflation remained at 3.5%, below the central bank’s medium-term target of 5%, due in part to tight monetary policy.
However, the report warns of growing fiscal pressures as deficits widen and debt servicing costs rise. It emphasizes the need for fiscal consolidation as outlined in Uganda’s FY2025/2026 budget.
Looking ahead, the World Bank projects a positive outlook for Uganda’s economy over the medium term. This forecast is supported by expectations of slower spending growth after elections, oil revenues starting in 2027, strong export performance, and sustained foreign direct investment inflows. Inflation is expected to remain low because of prudent monetary policy and stable commodity prices. Poverty rates are expected to decline further through 2026 and 2027.
The report identifies several risks that could affect these projections: possible fiscal slippages, delays in oil sector development, reduced overseas development assistance, global uncertainty affecting commodity prices and financial conditions, as well as climate shocks impacting rain-fed agriculture.
“Uganda’s growth remains strong, however economic activity is currently concentrated in low-productivity and climate-vulnerable agriculture and informal jobs, which offer limited opportunities for income growth and upward mobility,” said Francisca Ayodeji Akala, World Bank Country Manager for Uganda. “Transformation of the economy to higher value-added activities is needed to deliver on the country’s Ten-Fold Growth Strategy. Agro-industrialization can be a key cornerstone of this transformation, leveraging agriculture as a platform for industrial growth and job-creation.”
This edition of the update focuses on constraints facing agro-industrialization—a sector seen as having significant potential for job creation and inclusive economic growth.
“The building blocks to pursue the agro-industrial agenda in Uganda are consistent with the World Bank’s AgriConnect initiative, which aims to integrate smallholders into agribusiness and transform the sector into an engine of sustainable growth, job-creation, and food security,” said Armine Juergenliemk, Senior Agricultural Economist and co-author of the report. “This initiative opens opportunities for productive partnerships between the public and private sector to facilitate technology adoption, de-risk value chains, expand service delivery, and ultimately create more jobs in agriculture and the rural economy.”
The report recommends three main actions for advancing agro-industrialization:
1) Strengthen infrastructure by investing in climate-smart agricultural technologies; expanding irrigation; improving rural roads; developing skills; enabling digital solutions.
2) Improve policies by reforming regulations; supporting farmer cooperatives; encouraging competition among private firms; strengthening public institutions.
3) Mobilize private capital through innovative financing tools such as lease-to-own guarantees or blended finance; leveraging digital platforms; enhancing trade competitiveness.
The World Bank supports countries like Uganda by providing financing resources—such as loans—and technical expertise aimed at reducing poverty while fostering sustainable economic development across more than 190 countries [[source]](https://www.worldbank.org). Its initiatives often focus on strengthening social safety nets or improving infrastructure including transportation [[source]](https://www.worldbank.org). The organization operates under governance from its member states [[source]](https://www.worldbank.org).
Ajay Banga has served as president of The World Bank [[source]](https://www.worldbank.org).
